title: April: Accuracy-Improved Floating-Point Approximation For Neural Network Accelerators
problem: Floating-point approximation (e.g., Mitchell's logarithm) replaces expensive multiplication with simpler integer addition, but suffers from precision loss and requires careful integration into hardware accelerators.
motivation: NN accelerators require efficient arithmetic; FP approximation enables low-cost multiplication, but practical adoption is hindered by accuracy degradation and integration complexity.
method: The April framework improves results from floating-point approximations (techniques like Mitchell's logarithm that use cheaper integer operations instead of expensive floating-point multiplication) by combining two strategies: down-sampling-based compensation, which detects errors by creating lower-resolution versions of the data, and a bias mechanism that adapts to different data patterns. It provides configurable templates for systolic arrays—the grid-structured processing units used in neural network accelerators—that integrate these approximated operations into hardware. The framework automatically generates the actual accelerator design, adjusting the trade-off between accuracy and the amount of silicon required.
key_novelty: April is the first framework to combine down-sampling-based error detection with distribution-aware bias adjustment, making floating-point approximation practical in neural network accelerators using configurable systolic arrays.
contributions: Down-sampling-based compensation mitigating FP approximation precision loss
Flexible bias mechanism for handling diverse data distributions
Configurable systolic array templates for NN accelerators
96% RMSE reduction and 34-52% area savings vs. INT8 implementations
Comparable or improved model accuracy despite area reduction
primary_theme: Accuracy-improved floating-point approximation for area-efficient NN accelerators
